grammarNotes: In this unit, we’ll learn to describe pictures. Speaking of pictures, do you like to take pictures? Where do you save and put your pictures? In your computer, cell phone or in photo albums?
Look at the photo album of a church. The name of this church is Full Gospel Church. These pictures are from the church 9th anniversary party.

b. Our celebration group, “Elohim”, is dancing. (__1__)
d. The drama group is acting out a play. (__2__)
e. In the play, David is praying. (__5__)
f. The children are singing and dancing. (__4__)
Now look at these two sentences:
Which sentence expresses a habit? A or b?
Which sentence expresses a present action at the moment of speaking? A or b?
Sentence A expresses a habit, with the verb “prays” and the expression EVERY DAY.
Sentence B expresses an action that is present at the moment you are speaking.
DAVID IS PRAYING is the new verb tense of this lesson. This verb tense is the PRESENT CONTINUOUS.
The present continuous expresses an action at this moment, at the time of speaking, now (agora). It’s a temporary action.
You form this verb tense with
SUBJECT + BE + MAIN VERB (in the -ing form)
The main verb is in the -ing form. É equivalente em português ao GERÚNDIO: fazendo, falando, orando, etc.
In English, add -ing to the infinitive form of the verb.
When the verb ends in -e, drop the E and add -ing:
When the verb has one syllable and it ends in C+V+C, double the final consonant:
Here are some time expressions you use the present continuous:
now 	right now	today		tonight	at the moment
Look at the other pictures of the church party again. Memorize the actions. Say what they are doing. The verbs are DANCE – ACT OUT – HUG – SING – PRAY – CRY

grammarNotes: swimming • dancing • speaking • playing • driving • painting • using • cooking • doing • healing  • saying  • standing  • teaching
Let’s focus on the pronunciation of the -ing form.

Já falamos em outros vídeos sobre pronúncia que a relação entre as letras e os sons, fonemas, em inglês é um pouco irregular. Muitas vezes as letras de determinadas palavras não são pronunciadas, ou as letras são pronunciadas com outros sons.

Com a sílaba formada por -ing no final de verbos, não é diferente. Temos 3 letras, mas somente dois sons. A letra I tem som de /I/, como vimos num vídeo anterior e as letras -ng tem um som só: o som /N/. Esse é um som nasal e a posição do seu aparelho fonológico (boca, língua e céu da boca) é a mesma que a posição para os fonemas /g/ e /k/, só que o som vai sair pelo nariz.

Prepare a sua boca para pronunciar um /g/ ou /k/. Aí deixe o ar sair pelo nariz. O som /N/ nós temos em português. Tente pronunciar as palavras unha, ninho, minha. O som /N/ está na combinação das letras nh em português.
Repeat /N/. A sílaba toda é /Ing/. Sendo assim, a letra g não é pronunciada.
swimming • dancing • speaking • playing • driving • painting • using • cooking

In this lesson, we’ll learn more about verbs in the -ing form.
Remember the verbs with one syllable that end in CVC (consonant + vowel + consonant)? You double the consonant to form the -ing, right? For example:
Well, and when the verb has more than one syllable? It depends on the stressed syllable. For example, OPEN. It has two syllables:
The stress is on the first syllable. In this case, don’t double the consonant.
When the verb ends in CVC and that is a stressed syllable, double the consonant:
The word has two syllables. The stressed syllable is GIN. It’s a CVC. In this case, double the consonant.
In British English, when the verb ends in Vowel + L double the consonant.
Some verbs end in -ie. In this case, it’s irregular: drop the -e and add-ying
There are some verbs that you don’t use in the present continuous.
Normally, you don’t use the verb “need” (precisar) in the present continuous. Other verbs:
You don’t say “Are you understanding?” You say, “do you understand?”

grammarNotes: The name of this lesson is “The Armor of God”. We’ll learn about parts of the body.
In Ephesians 6.11, Paul says, “Put on the full armor of God”. “Full” means “complete, pleno”. “Put on” means “Wear”.
Here is the Full Armor of God:
The helmet of salvation in your head
The shield of faith in your arm
The belt of truth around your waist
The breastplate of righteousness on your chest
The preparation of the gospel on your feet

In Book 1, we learned about metaphors in the Bible. The Armor of God is also a metaphor. It is a comparison with the military clothes of the Roman empire at the time of Christ. It REPRESENTS God’s protection for your mind (sua mente) and your spirit (seu espírito). Nossas armas são a fé, a paz, o evangelho, a justiça...
The armor of God has six parts. Each part of the armor is in a part of your body (partes do seu corpo).
For example: the helmet of salvation on your HEAD.
Find the six parts of the body in the picture.
1. head 	2. Arm		3. Waist	4. Chest	5. Hand	6. feet

lessons.title: Grammar and Reading – Clothes around the world

tasks.instruction: Debbie shows the picture and reads the text to the student to describe the picture.

items.prompt: This picture shows a big group of people at a festival. They are sitting together at long tables and having a good time. Many people are smiling and laughing. They are wearing traditional German clothes. The women are wearing dresses (dirndls), and some men are wearing leather pants (lederhosen). They have a big glass of beer in their hands. They are raising their glasses and celebrating together. The people look very happy and friendly. It is a lively and fun atmosphere.

They are at a German beer festival, probably Oktoberfest in Munich. Oktoberfest is a big and lively festival in Germany. At Oktoberfest, people drink beer, eat traditional German food, listen to music, and dance. They often wear traditional clothes. People sit at long tables with their friends and family. They sing, laugh, and have fun together. There are also many rides and attractions.

grammarNotes: The name of this lesson is, ““The Scotsmen are wearing skirts.” We’ll talk about clothes around the world.
Look at these people. Where are they from?
1. Inuits from Alaska, Canada Greenland and Siberia
The climate determines the clothes people wear. The fur parka and the boots that Inuit (Eskimo*) people wear is very insulating – they protect them from the cold.
Muslim women wear long robes, because they believe it is a religious obligation.
Customs and traditions determine the clothes people wear, too. Scotsmen wear short skirts, called ‘kilts’, on special occasions.
Now look at these sentences. Are they True or False? Test your memory.
2. In picture 1, the Inuit woman is wearing a fur parka. (____)
5. In picture 3, the Scotsmen are wearing skirts. (____)
6. The Moroccan women are wearing long robes in picture 2. (____)
These sentences about clothes around the world are in the simple present tense or in the present continuous?
1. Inuits wear long robes. Simple Present
2. In picture 1, the Inuit woman is wearing a fur parka. Present Continuous
3. Scotsmen wear skirts every day. Simple Present
4. In Morocco, women wear skirts. Simple Present
5. In picture 3, the Scotsmen are wearing skirts. Present Continuous
6. The Moroccan women are wearing long robes in picture 2. Present Continuous
Let’s learn the difference between the simple present and the Present continuous tenses.
Scotsmen wear skirts on special occasions.
It describes a habitual action. It is in the simple present.
The Scotsmen in picture 3 are wearing skirts.
This sentence describes a present action at the moment of speaking. It is in the present continuous.

grammarNotes: There’s a cloud as small as a man’s hand
The name of this lesson is “There’s a cloud as small as a man’s hand.”. “Small” means “pequeno”, as we learned in Book 1.

There’s a passage in the Bible that has three different types of weather conditions. The Bible character is Elijah. Elijah was a prophet in the Old Testament. His story is in the book of 1 Kings. During Elijah’s time, there is a drought in Israel. “Drought”
means “seca”, that is, “no rain”. Elijah prays for rain. Do you remember that story?
Elijah went to the top of Carmel to pray for rain. Elijah told his servant,
Elijah sent him seven times. The seventh time, his servant said,
“There’s a cloud as small as a man’s hand.”
The sky got black with clouds, the wind rose and a heavy rain came on.
Where is Elijah praying in Picture 1?
He’s praying at the top of Carmel. (Carmel is a small mountain in that region)
What does Elijah tell his servant?
How many times does he send his servant?
What happens at the seventh time?
There’s a cloud as small as a man’s hand.
Does it rain at the end of the story?
That’s an incredible story about perseverance and faith! The four weather conditions are in Pictures 1, 2 and 3 – it’s sunny. In picture 4 it’s cloudy and windy and in Picture 5, it’s raining.
Now let’s look at the story again and this time, correct the sentences about the weather.
4. In picture 4, it’s sunny and windy.
It’s not sunny and windy. It’s cloudy and windy.
Now look at these two sentences based on the pictures 1 and 5 and on the text.
That’s the negative form of the present continuous tense. Similar to the verb to be, just add NOT after the verb.
